title: The Photo in the Group Chat
banner: Your ending came from your written answers, not from which option you picked.

scenes.title: Ping
scenes.description: A dark dorm room at night. You sit on the bed, seen from behind. Your phone lights your hands. A lamp glows on the desk.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tuesday, 11:40 pm. Your phone buzzes.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: Look who fell asleep on the shuttle.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It is Sarah. Mouth open. Bag on her lap.

lines.speaker: marco
lines.text: Ha! Legend.

lines.speaker: dev
lines.text: Send this to Hall B.

lines.speaker: screen
lines.text: 12 people are in Study Crew. Sarah is not one of them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Laughing faces fill the screen. You are not laughing.

scenes.title: Your Move
scenes.description: Close on your phone. Chat bubbles float in the dark, like paper cut-outs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody asked Sarah. She does not know.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: Isn't it perfect?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lisa is your friend. She is not cruel. She is laughing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You have a few seconds. What do you do?

scenes.title: Two More Groups
scenes.description: Three phones in a row, joined by paper strips like a paper chain. Each one shows the hidden photo.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By midnight, the photo has moved.

lines.speaker: dev
lines.text: Sent it to Hall B.

lines.speaker: marco
lines.text: Film Night too. They love it.

lines.speaker: screen
lines.text: Now it is in three chats. Anyone can save it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lisa has not written again. Your message sits there. Read.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lisa is silent. Others keep sending laughing faces.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sarah is asleep. She does not know.

scenes.title: Morning
scenes.description: The campus café, Wednesday morning. You stand behind Sarah in the queue. Marco and Dev are near the counter, looking at their phones.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Wednesday, 8:30 am. The campus café.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: People look at their phones. Then at Sarah.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Morning. Is something wrong with my bag?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She does not know. You do. Marco and Dev are three steps away.

scenes.title: Sarah Knows
scenes.description: A café table. Sarah sits across from you, and you are seen from behind. The light is softer.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Thank you for telling me first. It helps. A little.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You turn to Sarah and tell her. It is ten minutes late.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: You tried to stop it. I get that. I wish you had told me first.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sarah's hands shake a little.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: I do not want a fight. I just want it gone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She picks up her bag. She leaves her coffee.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The door opens. Lisa walks in, laughing. She sees your face. She stops.

lines.speaker: screen
lines.text: Lisa knows something is wrong.

scenes.title: Lisa's Excuse
scenes.description: A corner of the café by the door. Lisa faces you. You are seen from behind. The light is flat.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: What? It was one joke.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: I only shared it with close friends.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: I didn't expect anyone to forward it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She sounds sorry. She also sounds like she wants this to end.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: Come on. You know me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Friday. Two days later. You check the chats again.

options.label: Message Lisa privately.
options.sub: Ask her to take it down, just between you two.

beat.speaker: you
beat.text: Can you delete the photo? Sarah did not say yes.

beat.speaker: lisa
beat.text: It's a joke! She'll never see it.

beat.speaker: narrator
beat.text: Lisa did not say no. She did not delete it either.

options.label: Reply in the group chat.
options.sub: Say it where everyone can see.

beat.speaker: you
beat.text: Can we take this down? Sarah did not agree to it.

beat.speaker: marco
beat.text: Relax. It's funny.

beat.speaker: lisa
beat.text: Wow. Okay.

beat.speaker: narrator
beat.text: Two people agree with you. Others go quiet. Lisa goes quiet too.

options.label: Tell Sarah what is happening.
options.sub: Take her aside and tell her now.

beat.speaker: you
beat.text: Sarah, can we sit for a minute? Something was posted about you.

beat.speaker: sarah
beat.text: Posted? What?

beat.speaker: narrator
beat.text: You tell her. She asks to see it. Her face goes still.

beat.speaker: narrator
beat.text: Behind you, Marco and Dev still have it on their phones.

options.label: Ask the forwarders to delete it first.
options.sub: Ask Marco and Dev to take it down.

beat.speaker: you
beat.text: Marco, Dev. Please delete that photo. Now.

beat.speaker: marco
beat.text: Fine. Deleted.

beat.speaker: dev
beat.text: Others already saved it.

beat.speaker: narrator
beat.text: Two copies gone. Many are not. Sarah is still waiting for her coffee. She does not know.

d3.prompt: What do you say to Lisa?

options.label: Accept her excuse.
options.sub: Say you know she did not mean harm.

beat.speaker: you
beat.text: Okay. I know you did not mean for this to happen.

beat.speaker: lisa
beat.text: Thank you. I'll tell them to stop.

beat.speaker: narrator
beat.text: Lisa relaxes. Your friendship feels safe. Sarah has not heard from her.

options.label: Hold her responsible.
options.sub: Say the post was her choice.

beat.speaker: you
beat.text: You posted it. You did not ask Sarah. That part is on you.

beat.speaker: lisa
beat.text: That's not fair!

beat.speaker: lisa
beat.text: ...I didn't think.

beat.speaker: narrator
beat.text: Lisa goes red. She is hurt. She stops arguing.

why1.question: The photo is now in three chats. Who is responsible for what? Think about Lisa, the people who forwarded it, Sarah, and you. Write 2 to 4 sentences.
why1.helper: 2 to 4 sentences. There is no right answer, but reasons help.

followups.why1_fu_consequence: You said who did what. Now add one thing: what could happen to Sarah because of it?
followups.why1_fu_parties: You named one person. Who else played a part, and what was their part?
followups.why1_fu_split: Try to split it up. What is Lisa's part? What is the part of the people who forwarded it?

why1.harder: Now look from Sarah's side. She is not in the chat and she did not agree to the photo. What does she need from each person, and who can give it?
why1.nudge: Say a little more. Two or three sentences about who did what.
why1.ackHarder: Thanks. That adds a side the chat never heard.
why1.skipped: That is fine. Let's go on.

why2.question: Lisa says she only shared the photo with close friends and did not expect anyone to forward it. Do you agree with her? Give your reasons. Write 2 to 4 sentences.
why2.helper: 2 to 4 sentences. There is no right answer, but reasons help.

followups.why2_fu_reason: You said what you think. Now say why. What is one reason for your view?
followups.why2_fu_consequence: Think about Sarah. What changes for her if Lisa's excuse is accepted, and what changes if it is not? Add one to your answer.

why2.harder: Write the best reason someone could give for the opposite view. Then say if it changes your mind.
why2.nudge: Say a little more. Do you agree with Lisa? Give one reason.
why2.ackHarder: Thanks. It helps to hear the other side.
why2.skipped: That is fine. Let's go on.

A.title: A Way Forward
A.description: Warm, low sun on the library steps. Sarah, Lisa and you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sarah asks to meet on the library steps. Lisa is there too.

lines.speaker: lisa
lines.text: I posted a photo of you without asking. That was wrong. I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: sarah
lines.text: Thank you. I want it gone from every chat.

lines.speaker: screen
lines.text: Lisa, in all three chats: "I posted a photo of Sarah without asking. Please delete it. Do not share it."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Marco and Dev delete it. Some copies may still be out there. Sarah knows. She decides what happens next.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The steps are quiet. Sarah is not smiling. But she does not leave.

ask.question: Sarah is going to meet Lisa. What do you think she needs most from Lisa?

explain: Lisa said what she did and said sorry. Sarah did not have to ask for it. That is what made it possible to talk.
The photo came down in all three chats. Copies may still exist, so some risk stays with Sarah. That part could not be undone.
In your answers, you separated who did what: posting, forwarding and responding. That let you act without taking Sarah's choices from her.

B.title: Still Out There
B.description: Flat grey-blue light on the library steps. A bench with nothing on it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sarah does not come to tutorial. Her seat is empty.

lines.speaker: screen
lines.text: The photo is still in two chats. A new group has it now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lisa avoids you. Marco and Dev say it is old news.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody has said sorry. Sarah is carrying this alone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You open a message to Sarah. The cursor blinks.

ask.question: The photo is still in two chats. What do you think would help most now?

explain: In this story, nobody took full responsibility. Lisa's excuse stood. The forwarders stayed quiet. Sarah carried it alone.
Your answers named some of the people involved. They did not always say who owed what, or what it meant for Sarah. That makes it hard to know where to start.
It is not too late in the story. A clear sorry, a request to delete, and asking Sarah what she wants would all still help.
B.explainIfSkipped: You chose not to write some answers, so this ending comes from the story alone. Nobody in it said who owed what, and Sarah carried it alone.

choiceLines.d1_private: You messaged Lisa privately. That spared her in front of others. It also gave the photo more time to spread.
choiceLines.d1_group: You replied in the group. People saw you speak up. It also made Lisa feel called out.
choiceLines.d2_tell: You told Sarah first. She heard it from someone kind. She was also hurt in a public place.
choiceLines.d2_delete: You asked for deletions first. Some copies were stopped. Sarah heard later and wished she had been first.
choiceLines.d3_accept: You accepted Lisa's excuse. The friendship stayed calm. Lisa did not have to face what she did right away.
choiceLines.d3_hold: You held Lisa responsible. She had to face it. The friendship felt shaky for a while.

closing: There is no one right path. Another person might choose differently and still have good reasons. What matters here is being able to say who is responsible for what, and why.

reflect.offer: Want one more? A short, similar moment.
reflect.scenario: A friend sends you a screenshot of a private chat. In it, a classmate says something personal. Your friend says: "Pass it to the class group. Just for a laugh."
reflect.question: What do you think happens next if you pass it on? Write one or two sentences about who is affected and how.
reflect.ref_fu_next: Take one more step. What might happen after that?
reflect.ref_harder: What is one thing you could do at the start to change that outcome?
reflect.ref_ack: Thanks. That is the end of the story.
